capabilities.scope: On one operator-reported V1.2 sample, a battery-powered normal POWER-on boot from NOR reached the ESP_MOSAICO kernel and a single-user shell with an FFS memory-disk root. This does not establish NAND boot, full PSRAM read/write or general peripheral support.

On one operator-reported V1.2 sample, the net80211 scan cache reached 18 entries without ring or allocation failures. A strict SAE/PMF-required trial used kernel #33 and reused the prior radio object. SAE commit/confirm, supplicant Associated and net80211 RUN succeeded. Two multicast membership requests returned ENETRESET without resetting the join. The vendor then reported a four-way handshake timeout (reason 204), transitioned run to init and sent deauthentication; disconnect reason 204 followed. The capture does not establish EAPOL delivery or the failing handshake step. WPA_COMPLETED, negotiated PMF, DHCP/DNS and data exchange remain unverified.

Type-C USB-OTG ROM connection and complete 16 MiB NOR readback were verified with esptool 5.6.0. The board kernel has no S31 USB OTG role/controller integration. Dedicated package pads 44/45 are USB_D+/USB_D−, separate from GPIO44 LCD reset and GPIO45 audio PA enable. Host VBUS/CC role and power behavior are not verified; this does not establish EmberBSD USB support.

On one V1.2 sample, the standard CO5300 framebuffer/genfb/LVGL path displayed a visible interface after the published two-row RASET fix; the user also confirmed changing touch coordinates. This is one RAM-only scenario, not acceptance of other revisions. Touch orientation/calibration, audio playback and sustained operation remain unverified. Factory camera preview is vendor-firmware evidence; EmberBSD has a target-built SC101IOT sensor/DVP/video(4) path, but no physical EmberBSD frame has been captured. The mode table requires 20 MHz XCLK and names 15 fps; fitted oscillator frequency and actual frame rate are unmeasured. EmberBSD radio evidence includes scan and one failed strict SAE/PMF association attempt; WPA2-only authentication, DHCP and roaming remain unverified.

The BMI270, two BMM150 sensors and BQ27220 have native envsys drivers included in a target-linked ESP_MOSAICO_SC101IOT_WIFI kernel. Physical readings from these drivers have not been tested; prior BMI270 identification-register reads do not establish motion sampling.
S31 I2S/AHB-DMA and ES8311 drivers are present and the combined ESP_MOSAICO_SC101IOT_WIFI kernel linked. No physical playback or capture has been tested.

The board tree enables SPI3 and the published source adds a read-only NAND ID/status utility with a staged RV32 binary. It has not been run on hardware or installed in a root image; NAND data reads, ECC, bad-block management, filesystems and boot are not established.

On one V1.2 sample, the left-slot camera EEPROM descriptor had valid CRCs and hardware-version field 0x0102. The factory firmware separately reported SC101IOT PID 0xda4a and rendered a changing 1280 × 720 UYVY preview. The optional EmberBSD driver read SC101IOT PID 0xda4a at 0x68 in a RAM trial. Published source now adds a target-built 640 × 480 UYVY sensor/DVP/video(4) path, but no physical EmberBSD frame has been captured. Its mode table requires 20 MHz XCLK and names 15 fps; fitted oscillator frequency and actual frame rate are unmeasured. The factory and EmberBSD results apply only to this sample and do not establish sensor identity for other modules.
